prompt_text: Who is the best HVAC company in Atlanta to replace my air conditioner?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t one single “best” HVAC company for everyone — the right contractor depends on your home, budget, schedule, and the installer’s experience with the exact work you need. I can, however, help you pick a high-quality Atlanta contractor and find local options. Quick plan:

If you want me to pull local recommendations, please give your ZIP code. Otherwise, use the checklist and questions below when evaluating candidates.

What to require and check
- Licensing and insurance: ask for their Georgia HVAC/conditioned-air license number and verify it on the Georgia licensing site. Confirm general liability insurance and workers’ compensation.
- Written, itemized quote: model numbers, SEER rating, tonnage, labor, permit fees, disposal of old unit, and estimated timeline.
- Proper sizing and testing: insist on a Manual J load calculation (not “rule of thumb”) and a duct inspection/Manual D if ducts are being left in place.
- Permits & inspections: contractor should obtain all local permits and arrange final inspection.
- Warranties: get both equipment (manufacturer) and labor/installation warranty in writing; ask about warranty length and whether it’s transferable.
- Refrigerant: if replacing an older R‑22 system, confirm refrigerant type and cost implications.
- References & reviews: check Google, Yelp, BBB, Angi/HomeAdvisor and ask for recent local references for similar installs.

Questions to ask on the estimate
- Are estimates free? How long is the quote valid?
- Exact model number, SEER/HSPF (or efficiency rating), and capacity (tons).
- Will you perform a Manual J load calculation and inspect/measure existing ducts?
- What parts of the job are included (pad, refrigerant, line set, thermostat, permit)?
- Labor warranty length and what it covers.
- Timeline for scheduling and completion.
- Financing or rebate options (and help with utility or tax rebates).

Red flags
- Extremely low bid compared to others.
- No written quote or unwilling to provide model numbers.
- No license or insurance, or refuses to pull permits.
- High-pressure sales tactics or demands for large cash-up-front payments.

Typical cost range (Atlanta ballpark)
- Full central AC replacement: roughly $4,000–$9,000+ depending on system size, efficiency, ductwork needs, and complexity. Get at least three detailed quotes.

Next step I can do for you
- Provide 3–5 top-rated HVAC companies near you with recent review summaries and license checks — I just need your ZIP code.
- Or, if you already have 2–3 quotes, paste them and I’ll help compare them line-by-line.

Which would you like to do? (If local recommendations, please share your ZIP code.)
